Robert Boyle was an Anglo-Irish natural philosopher, chemist, physicist, and inventor. He was one of the most prolific figures in the scientific revolution and is often considered the first modern chemist, making him one of the founding fathers of modern chemistry and a pioneer of contemporary experimental scientific techniques. Boyle gave a very popular law which defines the inversely proportional connection between absolute pressure, and the volume of a gas in a closed system under constant temperature. Boyle was a polymath with diverse interests ranging from animal husbandry to underwater respiration, and from the study of ancient languages to finding ways of extending the human lifespan. Furthermore, Boyle had both the intellect and the financial resources to pursue such a wide research agenda.

13.1 Introduction All the states of matter; solid, liquid and gas, do not exhibit the same behavior on the application of heat. The applied heat cannot bring a significant change in pressure in the case of solid and liquid. But in the case of gas, applied heat brings out the change in temperature, volume as well as pressure. The properties, which the matter exhibits on the application of heat, are called thermal properties. Velocity, kinetic energy, mass, etc. are microscopic properties whereas pressure, temperature, volume, etc. are the macroscopic properties. Charles’ law, Boyle’s Law, Dalton’s law, etc. are the interrelationships among the values of thermal properties. By combining these laws in a special condition, the ideal gas equation can also be derived. The ideal gas equation describes the thermodynamic state of a matter at its equilibrium.

The kinetic molecular theory of a gas assumes that the gas molecules exchange energy and momentum during collisions with the wall of the container, and hence give pressure to the wall. This theory explains about macroscopic properties of gas.

13.2 Volume Coefficient and Pressure Coefficient Unlikely in the case of solid and liquid, gas shows simultaneous change in pressure and volume due to change in temperature. The study of simultaneous change in pressure and volume with temperature is a difficult one. Therefore, gas is heated either at a constant pressure or at a constant volume. Hence a gas has two thermal coefficients; pressure coefficient and volume coefficient.

The zero value of the absolute scale is called absolute zero temperature. At this temperature, the molecular motion stops, and the kinetic energy becomes zero. Also, the absolute temperature is directly proportional to the kinetic energy of its molecules and kinetic energy will never be negative. It means, the absolute temperature cannot be negative. Therefore, absolute zero temperature is the lowest possible temperature in the thermodynamic temperature scale. Hence, in other words, absolute zero temperature is defined as the lowest possible temperature that can exist in the universe. Till the date, the absolute zero temperature has not been practically measured, but the nearest approach is up to 10-8 K.
